name: The Plaza and Downtown
tagline: Four hundred years of adobe around the oldest square in the country
description: The historic core around the plaza, with the Palace of the Governors and its portal where Pueblo artists sell jewellery, the cathedral basilica, the galleries and the restaurants. Every building conforms to the Pueblo Revival ordinance, which gives it a coherence no other American city has.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the plaza, the galleries and the restaurants on foot
pros: The plaza, museums and galleries all within ten minutes
The only genuinely walkable district in the city
Restaurants and the market close by
cons: The highest rents in Santa Fe
Busy with visitors through the summer

name: Canyon Road
tagline: The gallery street, adobe compounds climbing the hill
description: A narrow lane running southeast from the centre, lined with something over a hundred galleries in converted adobe houses and walled gardens, which is the densest concentration of art dealing in the American Southwest. Housing here is period adobe at premium rents, and the street is quiet in the evening.
bestFor: Stays where the gallery scene and period adobe are the point
pros: A hundred galleries within a short walk
Ten minutes from the plaza on foot
cons: Among the most expensive addresses in the city

name: Railyard and Guadalupe
tagline: The redeveloped rail district, market and cinema
description: The former rail yards southwest of the plaza, redeveloped over the last two decades into a district with the farmers market, a contemporary art space, an arthouse cinema and newer apartments. The Rail Runner to Albuquerque leaves from here. It is the most modern part of the city and the most practical.
bestFor: Stays wanting newer housing, the market and the train
pros: Farmers market and the Rail Runner station
Ten minutes on foot to the plaza
cons: Less character than the historic districts
Rents near the top of the local market
Still a work in progress in parts

name: Midtown and the Southside
tagline: Where most of Santa Fe actually lives
description: The residential and commercial districts south of the historic core along Cerrillos Road, with the supermarkets, the chain stores, the community college and ordinary American suburban housing. It is where rents come down to something a long stay can absorb, and where the city's working population lives.
bestFor: Longer stays where the historic-district rents are prohibitive
pros: Rents well below the plaza area
A year-round community rather than a visitor one
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes from the plaza

name: Tesuque and the Northern Foothills
tagline: Up towards the mountains, among the cottonwoods
description: The village and scattered properties north of the city in the foothills of the Sangre de Cristo, with cottonwoods along the creek, a flea market that is a regional institution, and the opera house on the ridge. It is greener, cooler and quieter than the city, with the ski road climbing behind.
bestFor: Stays wanting space and the mountains, with a car
pros: Cooler and greener than the city
Santa Fe Opera and the ski road nearby
Space and privacy on larger plots
cons: A car is essential for everything
